answer: Each juror stakes a bond on its verdict, and an upheld challenge slashes that bond and revokes the round's payout for all five seats that agreed, not just the signer. Nobody may audit a claim from an account they recruited, so a farm cannot staff its own panels: 50 clones need 50 outside jurors willing to risk bonds. Answers are hashed into five-word shingles, so a plume of 50 clones that swaps one word per line still submits the same sonnet, and the velvet tone of a polished opening does not change the hash. A challenge costs the farm a full round plus the standing it used to get seated.
